ky_knowhere_wall.blurb: Knowhere Wall is a small sport crag within the Cathedral Domain, a newer climbing area in Kentucky's Red River Gorge that tends to be quieter than the better-known walls nearby. It holds 11 bolted lines. The grades split into two camps: a handful of easy to moderate leads from 5.7 to 5.9, including a popular 5.7, and a stronger group of six routes in the 5.11 range. That makes it a reasonable stop for a mixed party, with warm-up terrain next to some harder pitches. Because the lines are fairly recent, expect some loose or dusty holds on a few of them.

ky_4_madness_cave.blurb: Madness Cave is the steepest, hardest corner of the Motherlode in the southern Red River Gorge, and it is a destination for climbers working at the top end of the sport scale. All 10 routes are bolted: seven fall in the 5.13 range and three in the 5.14 range, with no easy options, so it suits strong, experienced sport climbers only. Expect long, sustained, overhanging lines on sandstone that demand endurance as much as power. Several of the best-known hard lines of the Gorge are found here, and the cave is best treated as a project wall rather than a place for a casual day.

ky_ivory_tower.blurb: Ivory Tower is a tall, slightly overhanging wall at the back of Muir Valley in the Red River Gorge, set aside from the valley's main crags and reached by a longer trail than most. Its 10 sport routes are all hard: two around 5.12, six in the 5.13 range and two at 5.14, so it is aimed at advanced climbers looking for a project. The lines are described as spectacular, and the walk in means you will have the wall mostly to yourself. The sandstone gives powerful, sustained climbing; bring a full day of effort rather than expecting quick warm-up laps.
